agree.reason: The memo is clear and sets a checkpoint, and it handles the colleague with care, but it leaves the cash gap as an open promise ('I will propose'), which gives the two ad-background members room to resist.

honest.reason: The memo reads the two ad figures as two years apart and calls the fall 'about 20% a year', but the facts show a 36% drop in a single year, so both the trend and the projections built on it are wrong, even though the error makes the case look weaker rather than stronger.

works_the_facts.reason: The membership numbers are derived correctly (875 members, 6.25% of the list, $20,350, about $52k collected in the first year), but the ad projections rest on the misread rate; the true pace would put 2027 ads near $54k, roughly level with first-year membership cash, and that stronger true version is lost.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is presented as falling, which is the right frame, but the memo understates how fast ads are falling ($67k/$54k instead of about $54k/$34k), so the alternative looks much better than the facts show.

qualification.reason: The June 30 checkpoint names a date, a number (550 members) and a consequence (options at the July meeting), and cancellations are tracked at every board meeting, though the hedge on the cash gap has no figure or date attached.

objections.reason: It deals with cancellations, first-year cash and the 11-year colleague, which are what the ad-background members will raise, but it never considers a hybrid option or explains why ads can't be kept alongside membership, and its stated cash gap is larger than the true one.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted memo of about one page with a clear decision request and short sections, as the brief asked.
